identity.description: Close is a CRM with built-in calling, email, SMS, automation and AI, with a public REST API, webhooks and a remote MCP server.

auth.oauth_flows: OAuth 2.0 authorization flow for user-facing integrations; MCP supports OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration.
auth.token_refresh: offline_access scope granted to OAuth apps.
auth.scopes_notes: OAuth apps are granted all.full_access and offline_access scopes. MCP uses Close-Scope header: mcp.read, mcp.write_safe, mcp.write_destructive.

access.production_restrictions: OAuth apps are Private by default; to let other Close customers authorize it you must request to make it public and optionally get listed.

read_ops: List and read leads, contacts, opportunities, activities
write_ops: Create/update leads, contacts, activities, custom data
api.rate_limits: Rate limits apply to all endpoints; handle 429 with exponential backoff.
api.limitations: OpenAPI spec is experimental; event log covers only the last 30 days; max 40 webhook subscriptions per org.

claims.quote: API Keys — Best for scripts, internal tools, and server-side integrations. Use HTTP Basic Auth with your API key as the username and an empty password.
API keys can be created and managed in your Close account under Settings → Developer → API Keys .
Dev organizations work identically to standard Close organizations but have no subscription fees.
Close uses industry-standard REST conventions with predictable URL structures, standard HTTP methods, and JSON request/response bodies.
Activities Calls, emails, notes, SMS, meetings, and other interactions logged on leads.
The MCP server URL is https://mcp.close.com/mcp and has “HTTP Streamable” and “OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)” support.
Webhooks allow a subscription URL to be configured that we will POST event data to as it is added to the Event Log .
Close’s Python Wrapper (Officially maintained by Close)
OAuth apps are Private by default, meaning only members of your own Close organization can authorize them.

open_questions: Whether API access requires a paid plan after the free trial ends is not stated.
Specific numeric rate limits are not stated in the provided sources.
